<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Alma S. Adams, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Adelita S. Grijalva>: The bill specifies what would have to be included in an application for funding, and it would prohibit the Secretary from requiring any additional information. Notably, the new State Facilities Aid Program would establish priorities where none exist in current law. These priorities would favor states that are already more charter friendly than other states. It would also favor states that already provide support for charter school facilities. Together, these priorities would effectively ensure that the number of charter schools would continue to grow quickly in such states. While the new program would permit up to five percent of the federal grant to be used for evaluations, technical assistance, and dissemination of information, it would not require the funds to be used in that manner.
This new program would broaden the use of federal funding, establish and maintain a permanently high federal share amount, allow for the state to avoid any share of the funding by partnering with any organization(s), and require no oversight or evaluation to determine how the program is working or the effects of the program. Despite the fact that taxpayer dollars are at stake, the Republican Majority would design, construct, and implement a new program without any sort of transparency, accountability, or oversight mechanisms to ensure the efficacy of their creation.
DEMOCRATIC AMENDMENTS OFFERED DURING THE MARKUP OF
H.R. 7086
Committee Democrats proffered two amendments to improve the bill. These amendments would have required fair wages be paid to workers on all projects funded under the programs in this bill and would have required an evaluation of the new State Facilities Aid Program created by the Republican Majority. Committee Republicans rejected both Democratic amendments that were considered.

CONCLUSION
H.R. 7086 would expand charter school facilities support and replace the current Per-Pupil Facilities Grants with an entirely new program without guardrails, transparency, or accountability, and it would take funding away from charter schools themselves. For the reasons stated above, all Committee Democrats present opposed H.R. 7086 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on January 21, 2026. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Suzanne Bonamici,
Alma S. Adams,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Adelita Grijalva,
Members of Congress.
